summary: The Final Report decides most of the Top 50 judgement: it alone can show Portfolio Analysis (projections under varying outcomes), Articulation and the co-sponsor part of Creativity, and the Top 50 is picked on the IPS and Final Report. The window is 25 days (instructions Tue 10 Nov Sydney, due Sat 5 Dec 09:00) and Knox's term ends Thu 3 Dec; last year 30 of 63 dated comments in the Knox report came in the final two days, with an instruction to make up stories, so the team must pre-build before 9 Nov. Forecast (from Wharton's own 2022-24 specs and last year's doc): title page, a ~150-word team reflection and maybe an advisor reflection, Portfolio-at-a-Glance with WInS and recommended snapshots plus a same-or-different answer, 5-8 pages of report details, APA Works Cited recording AI use, and a page range with a minimum as well as a maximum. Evidence the team must start collecting now is missing: the trade log is blank, the journal stops 7 Oct, the AI log has no entries 1-15 Oct, and no WInS history, source list or post-freeze tracking exists. The ladder-cost conflict is a basis difference: $294.5k prices the payment dates, while Caplet's holdings cost $297.8k-$298.6k on 15 Oct; use the holdings basis and one valuation date (the 6 Nov close), and present January as roughly break-even because the $1.4k-$2.2k room is smaller than one day's move and than the gap between two sensible methods. The AI kit's 'note-in-Final-Report' backlog includes STRIPS-basis tables without banners and must not be imported. After the freeze, the right implementation evidence is the ladder tracking the payments, and about $1,539 of November coupons will sit as cash, conflicting with V5's 'income reinvested'. Finale readiness is low because key calls and numbers came from AI; the lens gives 30 forecast judge questions with what a good answer must cover and a no-laptop test. Commit 412e9e3 adds useful Final Report numbers and the October curve, but its headline ladder cost is on the wrong basis and its [AI] suggestion rule is riskiest in the Articulation and co-sponsor sections.

findings.problem: Instructions arrive Tue 10 Nov Sydney; the report is due Sat 5 Dec 09:00. Knox Term 4 ends Thu 3 Dec (Presentation Day) and Fri 4 Dec is a staff day, so the advisor and administrator are hardest to reach at the end. Last year 30 of 63 dated comments in the Knox Final Report doc came on 11-12 Dec (deadline 12 Dec), including an instruction to make up stories. Last year's window was 46 days; this year's is 25. Starting on 10 Nov would repeat that pattern with less time.

findings.title: Use one valuation date and the holdings basis for every Final Report number; the room under $300k is inside model noise
findings.problem: The $294.5k (number sheet) and $298.6k (lenses) ladder costs use the same 15 Oct curve and payments; they differ because the sheet prices the payment dates while Caplet's holdings mature 0.5-10.5 months earlier (about $3.4k), plus forward vs unchanged curve (about $0.8k). For Caplet's plan only the holdings basis is right. Even then the room ($1.4k-$2.2k) is smaller than one day's move ($2.7k on 15 Oct), the 5-15 Oct range ($6.5k) and the gap between a bootstrap and a simple par-yield method ($1.4k). A precise 'surplus' claim can be false by the time it is read.
evidence: oct16/research/KB_verify/num/reconcile.py re-run on caplet-latest/competition/official_market_data/daily-treasury-rates_2026-10.csv: payment dates fwd $294,461 (room $5,539); holdings fwd $297,847 ($2,153, 7.4bp); holdings unchanged $298,628 ($1,372, 4.7bp)

Describe January's purchase as roughly break-even with V5's rule that the 2028 deposit completes the ladder first. Re-derive or drop the '1 case in 3' figure. Every student can explain why $294.5k is not Caplet's number.
